title: Fast and Fresh Veg Sides: Blanching, Salt-Bruising, and Pan-Steaming with Beurre Monte Finish
summary: In this ATK segment, Lan Lam demonstrates a restaurant-inspired approach to keeping vegetables vibrant and fast on the plate by rethinking prep rather than reinventing cooking. The lesson walks through blanching vegetables to near doneness and shocking them in an ice bath to preserve texture and flavor, followed by salt-bruising (yamitsuki-inspired) cabbage to concentrate sweetness. It then shows a pan-steaming technique for broccoli/broccolini using a small amount of water and a lid to generate steam, finishing florets with a butter-based beurre monte sauce laced with lemon zest, thyme, shallot, and pepper. The video also covers meal-prep strategies for blanching ahead, reheating methods, and practical salt ratios for flavorful, quickly served veg alongside proteins.

sections.description: The cabbage is salted heavily and massaged to bruise the leaves, drawing out moisture and concentrating flavor. After 15 minutes, excess salt is rinsed away to maintain crispness. This technique evokes yamitsuki cabbage and similar salted, lightly massaged veggies used in pickling-style textures.

sections.description: Steve Dunn's pan-steaming method uses a modest amount of water in a 12-inch skillet and a lid to surround vegetables with steam. Broccolini is segmented and peeled by stalk width to ensure even cooking, then finished with a butter-based aromatics blend for depth of flavor.
